## What's new

Threadnote 5.3.4 makes index preparation clearer, keeps longer workflow-memory writes trackable, and improves process and development-workflow visibility.

### Prepare lexical and semantic recall together

`threadnote index rebuild` waits for both lexical search and semantic recall to be ready for the inputs it inspected. Source, model, or authorization drift is reported instead of presenting an outdated rebuild as current.

### Track longer memory writes

Longer workflow-memory writes can return a trackable pending operation instead of holding the client open. They finish only after the canonical write and required lexical checks complete. Explicit synchronization and repair commands retain their requested completion behavior.

### See which processes are doing the work

Manager shows CPU and memory use with workspace, client, and foreground/background lane context, including owned workers. This makes active work and resource use easier to follow.

### Keep development reviews tied to current source

Development workflows distinguish implementation from independent correctness, simplicity, and specialist reviews. Base and stacked-proof checks keep evidence tied to current source while preserving phase and review history.
